verdicts.one_liner: Quotes accurate; written PDF f=(1/a)exp(-Dt/a) has mean a (scale=a in numpy) but Gillespie/target need mean 1/a (scale=1/a); target reproduces exactly as std_exp/A=0.0004090657. Formula contradicts the 'rate=sum propensities' prose.

Contract is silent on whether the event crossing T is recorded; target excludes it (n=3467, last_t<T), so a naive while-t<T loop records one extra row -> hard allclose shape failure. Genuine ambiguity.
'rounded up to one decimal point' is round-to-nearest in targets (0.6283->0.6, not ceil's 0.7); literal ceil reading fails 53.3/53.4. Real but minor wording defect.

summary: All three findings confirmed: two D10 wording/formula contradictions (exponential PDF scale and 'rounded up' meaning round-to-nearest) and one D4 unspecified T-recording boundary. The exponential-scale defect (53.1) is the most serious and was independently reproduced (target = std_exp/A exactly); fixing the three wording points makes the problem fully fair.
